mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly FEDFUNDS rate above the prior month's level precedes a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to expectations of tighter credit conditions.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > previous month FEDFUNDS by > 0.25 percentage points
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain positive despite FEDFUNDS increase, or FEDFUNDS rise is not statistically significant (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 4%, labor market slack increases, reducing expected wage growth and depressing 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive when UNRATE crosses below 4%, or the effect is not statistically significant (IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly increases in HOUST (household spending) of at least 2% over the prior month predict a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as consumer confidence strengthens.
failure_condition: No significant positive 20-day returns after qualifying HOUST increases, or IC < 0.1 over 1000 instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in INDPRO (industrial production) index below 95 triggers a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as weak manufacturing signals contractionary expectations.
failure_condition: INDPRO remains above 95 during contractionary regimes with positive 20-day returns, or effect is not robust (IC > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS rises by more than 0.5% in a single month, followed by two consecutive months of similar increases, the S&P 500 shows negative 60-day forward returns as investors anticipate higher rates.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by > 0.5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain positive despite the pattern, or the pattern is not statistically significant (IC > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in PAYEMS (employment) and UNRATE below 5% indicate labor market stress, leading to negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive when both proxies decline, or interaction effect is not significant (IC > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in GDPC1 (GDP) of at least 3% for two consecutive months predicts a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as growth expectations rise.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > previous month GDPC1 by ≥ 3.0% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: No significant positive 60-day returns after qualifying growth, or IC < 0.05 over 1000 instances.

mechanism_narrative: When RSAFS (retail sales) falls by more than 10% in a month compared to the prior month, the S&P 500 shows a negative 5-day forward return reflecting weak consumer demand.
failure_condition: 5-day returns are positive during contraction, or the effect is not robust (IC > 0.2).
